hook_text: Two teams. Same pay, same shop, same rules. One team keeps its people. The other loses half of them. Why?
clip_script: Supervisor A greets everyone by name, explains the plan, corrects mistakes quietly and says thank you for good ideas. Supervisor B arrives late, shouts, has favourites and blames people in front of customers. A year later: Team A lost one of eight people. Twelve and a half percent. Team B lost four of eight. Fifty percent. Half the team gone, plus more mistakes, more absences, more complaints. Good managers are honest and fair, communicate clearly, know the work, see the big picture, and pick the right style: firm in a fire drill, asking for ideas when there is time. The difference between the teams was never the shop. It was the manager.
visual_style: A whiteboard split screen of two shop aisles, team members as stick figures, one side calm and full, the other with figures walking out of the door, and two turnover dials at twelve and a half and fifty percent.
mood: Relatable and thought-provoking, with a clear lesson.
pacing: Two quick character sketches, a pause on the numbers, then a confident close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and score a manager you know.
